meta.dc:rights: The Government of the Hong Kong Special Administrative Region

main.longTitle: An Ordinance to provide for the playing and singing of the national anthem, for the protection of the national anthem, and for the promotion of the national anthem, in Hong Kong; and for incidental matters.

preamble.name: preamble
preamble.heading: Preamble
preamble.recital: WHEREAS—(1)the national anthem of the People’s Republic of China is a symbol and sign of the People’s Republic of China;(2)all individuals and organizations should respect the national anthem, preserve the dignity of the national anthem, and play and sing the national anthem on appropriate occasions; and(3)an Ordinance is to be enacted to preserve the dignity of the national anthem, to regulate the playing and singing, the broadcast and the use of the national anthem, to enhance citizen awareness of the People’s Republic of China, and to promote patriotism:

enactingFormula.content: NOW, THEREFORE, it is enacted by the Legislative Council as follows—

main.editorialNote: ____________________Editorial Note:This instrument was not given a chapter number under the Legislation Publication Ordinance (Cap. 614). An unofficial reference number, however, is assigned to this instrument in Hong Kong e-Legislation (https://www.elegislation.gov.hk) for identification purpose. This also enables users to carry out a search by reference to the unofficial reference number.

section.name: s1
section.heading: Short title
section.content: This Ordinance may be cited as the National Anthem Ordinance.

subsection.def: national anthem (國歌) means “March of the Volunteers” (a translation of《義勇軍進行曲》), the national anthem of the People’s Republic of China under the Constitution of the People’s Republic of China;
national flag (國旗) has the same meaning as in the National Flag and National Emblem Ordinance (116 of 1997).

subsection.leadIn: In this Ordinance, a reference to the lyrics, and the score, of the national anthem is a reference to—

paragraph.name: a
paragraph.content: the lyrics, and the score, set out in the stave notation of the national anthem in Schedule 1; or

paragraph.name: b
paragraph.content: the lyrics, and the score, set out in the numbered musical notation of the national anthem in Schedule 2.

subsection.leadIn: In this Ordinance, except in section 5, a reference to playing and singing the national anthem includes—

paragraph.name: a
paragraph.content: singing the national anthem;

paragraph.name: b
paragraph.content: playing the national anthem on musical instruments; and

paragraph.name: c
paragraph.content: playing a recording of the national anthem.

part.name: P2
part.heading: Playing and Singing of National Anthem

section.name: s3
section.heading: Standard for playing and singing
section.content: The national anthem must be played and sung in a way that is in keeping with its dignity.

subsection.content: This section applies in relation to an occasion on which the national anthem is played and sung.

subsection.leadIn: While the national anthem is being played and sung, the etiquette to be followed by the persons who take part in or attend the occasion is—

paragraph.name: a
paragraph.content: to stand solemnly and deport themselves with dignity; and

paragraph.name: b
paragraph.content: to not behave in a way disrespectful to the national anthem.

section.name: s5
section.heading: Occasions on which national anthem must be played and sung

subsection.content: On each occasion set out in Schedule 3, the national anthem must be played and sung.
The Chief Executive in Council may, by notice published in the Gazette, amend Schedule 3.

In this section, a reference to the national anthem being played and sung is a reference to the national anthem being played on musical instruments in accordance with the standard score, or an official recording of the national anthem being played, for the singing of the national anthem.

subsection.def: official recording (官方錄音), in relation to the national anthem, means a recording of the national anthem provided for the purposes of this section on a website of the Government*;
standard score (標準曲譜), in relation to the national anthem, means a score of the national anthem provided for the purposes of this section on a website of the Government*.

tr.td: See the website of the Constitutional and Mainland Affairs Bureau of the Government of the Hong Kong Special Administrative Region: https://www.cmab.gov.hk.

section.name: s6
section.heading: Offence of misuse of national anthem

subsection.leadIn: The national anthem, or the lyrics or score of the national anthem, must not be used—

paragraph.name: a
paragraph.content: in a trade mark or commercial advertisement;

paragraph.name: b
paragraph.content: at a private funeral event; or

paragraph.name: c
paragraph.content: on an occasion, at a place, or for a purpose, prescribed under subsection (5).

subsection.content: The national anthem must not be used as background music in a public place.
A person commits an offence if the person, without reasonable excuse, uses the national anthem, or the lyrics or score of the national anthem, in contravention of subsection (1) or (2).

subsection.leadIn: A person who commits an offence under subsection (3) is liable on conviction—

paragraph.name: a
paragraph.content: for a contravention of subsection (1)(a)—to a fine at level 5; or

paragraph.name: b
paragraph.content: otherwise—to a fine at level 2.

subsection.content: The Chief Executive in Council may, by notice published in the Gazette, prescribe an occasion, place or purpose, for the purposes of subsection (1)(c).

subsection.def: public place (公眾場所) means a place to which the public or a section of the public may or are permitted to have access from time to time, whether by payment or otherwise.

subsection.leadIn: A person commits an offence if, with intent to insult the national anthem, the person publicly and intentionally—

paragraph.name: a
paragraph.content: alters the lyrics or score of the national anthem; or

paragraph.name: b
paragraph.content: plays and sings the national anthem in a distorted or disrespectful way.

subsection.content: A person commits an offence if the person publicly and intentionally insults the national anthem in any way.

subsection.leadIn: A person commits an offence if, with intent to insult the national anthem, the person intentionally publishes—

paragraph.name: a
paragraph.content: altered lyrics or an altered score of the national anthem; or

paragraph.name: b
paragraph.content: the national anthem played and sung in a distorted or disrespectful way.

subsection.content: A person commits an offence if, with intent to insult the national anthem, the person intentionally publishes the insulting in any way of the national anthem.

subsection.leadIn: Except as provided under subsection (3) or (4), a person does not commit an offence under this section by publishing—

paragraph.name: a
paragraph.content: altered lyrics or an altered score of the national anthem;

paragraph.name: b
paragraph.content: the national anthem played and sung in a distorted or disrespectful way; or

paragraph.name: c
paragraph.content: the insulting in any way of the national anthem.

subsection.content: A person who commits an offence under this section is liable on conviction to a fine at level 5 and to imprisonment for 3 years.

subsection.leadIn: Proceedings may only be commenced for an offence under this section before whichever is the earlier of the following—

paragraph.name: a
paragraph.content: the end of the period of 1 year after the date on which the offence is discovered by, or comes to the notice of, the Commissioner of Police;

paragraph.name: b
paragraph.content: the end of the period of 2 years after the date on which the offence is committed.

subsection.def: insult (侮辱), in relation to the national anthem, means to undermine the dignity of the national anthem as a symbol and sign of the People’s Republic of China;

publish (發布) includes—(a)to communicate to the public in any form, including speaking, writing, printing, displaying notices, broadcasting, screening and playing of tapes or other recorded material; and(b)to distribute, disseminate or make available to the public.

section.name: s8
section.heading: Music, words or score to be regarded as national anthem, or its lyrics or its score
section.leadIn: For the purposes of this Part—

paragraph.name: a
paragraph.content: a piece of music (whether or not including words intended to be sung or spoken with the music) is to be regarded as the national anthem if the piece of music so closely resembles the national anthem as to lead to the reasonable belief that the piece of music is the national anthem or a part of the national anthem;

paragraph.name: b
paragraph.content: words (whether or not in writing) are to be regarded as the lyrics of the national anthem if the words so closely resemble the lyrics of the national anthem as to lead to the reasonable belief that the words are the lyrics of the national anthem or a part of the lyrics; and

paragraph.name: c
paragraph.content: a score is to be regarded as the score of the national anthem if the score so closely resembles the score of the national anthem as to lead to the reasonable belief that the score is the score of the national anthem or a part of the score of the national anthem.

section.name: s9
section.heading: Inclusion in primary and secondary education

subsection.leadIn: The Secretary for Education must give directions for the inclusion of the national anthem in primary education and in secondary education—

paragraph.name: a
paragraph.content: to enable the students to learn to sing the national anthem; and

subparagraph.content: on the history and spirit of the national anthem; and
on the etiquette for playing and singing the national anthem.

subsection.def: primary education (小學教育) has the meaning given by section 3(1) of the Education Ordinance (Cap. 279);
secondary education (中學教育) has the meaning given by section 3(1) of the Education Ordinance (Cap. 279).

section.name: s10
section.heading: Inclusion in sound broadcasting and domestic television programme services

subsection.content: This section applies if, under the terms and conditions of a broadcasting licence, the licensee may be required by a determination or direction of the Communications Authority to broadcast announcements in the public interest, or to include material in the public interest, in the licensed service.

By a determination or direction that has been made in relation to the broadcasting licence, the licensee may be required to broadcast the national anthem by an announcement in the public interest, or material in the public interest, in the licensed service.

The Communications Authority must make a determination or direction in relation to the broadcasting licence, requiring the licensee to broadcast the national anthem by an announcement in the public interest, or material in the public interest, in the licensed service on each date that is or may be stipulated under subsection (4).
The Chief Executive may stipulate a date for the purposes of subsection (3).

paragraph.name: a
paragraph.content: must be published in the Gazette as soon as practicable after it is made; and

paragraph.name: b
paragraph.content: is not subsidiary legislation.

subsection.def: broadcasting licence (廣播牌照) means—(a)a licence granted under section 13C(2) of the Telecommunications Ordinance (Cap. 106), or such a licence renewed under section 13E(2) of that Ordinance; or(b)a licence granted under sections 8(1) and 10(1) of the Broadcasting Ordinance (Cap. 562), or such a licence extended or renewed under section 11(1) of that Ordinance;
Communications Authority (通訊事務管理局) means the Communications Authority established by section 3 of the Communications Authority Ordinance (Cap. 616).

section.name: s11
section.heading: Application of laws of Hong Kong

subsection.content: Offences in relation to the national anthem in Hong Kong are investigated, and persons are prosecuted, according to the laws of Hong Kong.
If there are inconsistencies between this Ordinance and the National Anthem Law, this Ordinance is to be interpreted and applied as a special application or adaptation of the National Anthem Law.

subsection.def: National Anthem Law (《國歌法》) means the Law of the People’s Republic of China on National Anthem, adopted at the 29th Meeting of the Standing Committee of the Twelfth National People’s Congress on 1 September 2017.

section.name: s12
section.heading: Enactments amended
section.content: The enactments specified in Divisions 2 and 3 are amended as set out in those Divisions.
